findings.title: The operation matrix does not enumerate the resource identifiers that drive relationship authorization

sourceEvidence.explanation: The handler consumes postId, answerId, and commentId and persists them, while its assigned matrix row declares an empty resourceInputs array.
The handler consumes targetType, targetId, and postId and begins target mutation, while its matrix row declares no resource inputs.
The route parameter postId selects the protected parent, but the matrix row declares no resource inputs.
postId selects the post and causes a mutation before the protected post is returned, but all three method rows declare no resource inputs.
Creation accepts courseId, syllabusItemId, and tagIds and persists the course/syllabus associations, but its matrix row lists GET feed parameters instead of these mutation resources.

findings.impact: The design calls the matrix the operation-level source of truth and requires future cases to bind to it. Missing or incorrect resource inputs leave no exact per-operation obligation to resolve a flag target, moderation target, post, course, syllabus item, or tag through the authorized persisted parent. An implementation or verification plan could therefore satisfy the stated matrix while retaining cross-course or mismatched-child access.
findings.recommendation: Revise each affected operation row to enumerate every route, query, and body identifier that selects a protected resource. State the exact lookup chain and predicates for each method, including answer/comment to post, syllabusItem to course, tag validity, course membership/assignment, post visibility, and uniform safe 404 behavior. Regenerate the request-bound matrix and case-set digest for fresh review.

findings.title: Digest authorization is ambiguous between the existing ADMIN-only contract and the revised all-KX-role matrix

sourceEvidence.explanation: The assigned source shows an explicit ADMIN-only authorization rule.

After the ADMIN check, the operation reads global recent posts and creates a digest notification for the actor; the revised matrix instead grants the generic KX role set without stating that this is an intentional behavior change.

findings.impact: The revised design simultaneously requires preservation of legitimate existing behavior and assigns STUDENT and instructor aliases to this endpoint. Implementers cannot determine whether non-Admin invocation must remain forbidden or become supported. The ambiguity can broaden an administrative operation and invalidates a trustworthy authorization test oracle.
findings.recommendation: Obtain an explicit product/security decision for this operation and encode it in the matrix. If existing behavior is preserved, set normalRoles to ADMIN and define its ICS eligibility. If self-service digest creation is intentionally introduced, document the approved behavior change, post visibility filters, rate/idempotency rules, and actor-only notification effect before implementation review.

implementationRisks.title: Current shared role normalization converts SUPER_USER and every unknown role into STUDENT

sourceEvidence.explanation: Only ADMIN and instructor aliases are recognized; every other role is returned as STUDENT.
Every assigned handler obtains its role through the unsafe normalizer.
Eligibility is then based on the session user's institute and returns the normalized role, so an ICS SUPER_USER can reach handlers as a STUDENT unless an individual handler happens to require staff.

implementationRisks.impact: The unimplemented baseline cannot enforce the revised UNKNOWN fail-closed rule or the mandatory SUPER_USER 403 ceiling across the assigned KX operations.
implementationRisks.recommendation: Implement an explicit recognized-role result including SUPER_USER and UNKNOWN, make UNKNOWN unauthorized, and require every assigned handler to reject SUPER_USER/UNKNOWN before protected parsing, reads, writes, serialization, notifications, EXP, or other effects.

implementationRisks.title: Current handlers do not consistently enforce persisted course visibility and parent-child binding

sourceEvidence.explanation: A flag is created directly from caller IDs without resolving the selected answer/comment/post to an accessible parent post.
GET checks only the actor-owned follow row and does not establish that the requested post or tag is visible and valid for the actor.
POST resolves only post existence/deletion and does not enforce course-linked enrollment, instructor assignment, or Admin authority.
The parent post is resolved without its course/institute relationship before answer creation.
A caller-supplied courseId is added directly to the feed query without first proving enrollment, assignment, or Admin course authority.
courseId, syllabusItemId, and tagIds are persisted without resolving their mutual relationship or the actor's course authority.

implementationRisks.impact: Recognized ICS users may read or mutate course-linked KX resources outside their enrollment or assignment, create mismatched course/syllabus links, or attach flags/follows to inaccessible resources.
implementationRisks.recommendation: Implement the revised KX capability as persisted, query-constraining parent resolution before effects. Resolve all child IDs through the authorized post/course, enforce approved enrollment or instructor assignment/Admin authority, and return a uniform safe 404 for foreign or mismatched resources.

implementationRisks.title: Current moderation operations grant institute-wide staff access without target-course assignment checks

sourceEvidence.explanation: Authorization stops at normalized ADMIN or INSTRUCTOR role.
The transaction updates caller-selected post, answer, or comment IDs and writes an audit row without first resolving the target's actual parent, ICS author, or instructor course assignment.
Any eligible normalized instructor or Admin receives global pending flags and recent actions, including reporter email and content, with no target-course authorization constraints.
Any normalized INSTRUCTOR is treated as staff and may delete any selected post, without checking course assignment or the distinct course-less-board moderation rule.

implementationRisks.impact: An ICS instructor can moderate, deanonymize, inspect reporter data, or delete course-linked content outside courses they teach. Caller-supplied postId in the moderation audit can also be unrelated to an answer/comment target.
implementationRisks.recommendation: Resolve each moderation target to its actual post, course, and author before returning private queue data or mutating. Require assignment for course-linked content, apply the explicit course-less-board rule, constrain Admin eligibility as designed, and derive audit postId from the resolved target rather than accepting an unrelated value.

implementationRisks.title: Current detail GET mutates viewCount before proving resource visibility or existence

sourceEvidence.explanation: The handler increments viewCount immediately from postId and suppresses update errors before loading and authorizing the post.
The not-found/deleted decision occurs only after the attempted mutation.

implementationRisks.impact: Requests for deleted, foreign, or otherwise unauthorized posts can cause a persistent side effect before the required safe 404 and relationship decision.
implementationRisks.recommendation: Resolve the post through an authorization-constrained query first. Increment viewCount only after successful visibility authorization, and ensure denied or absent resources produce no effects.

implementationRisks.title: Current answer and post creation trigger gamification outside the authorization/write transaction

sourceEvidence.explanation: Answer creation and notification commit first; EXP is then attempted through a separate helper and errors are suppressed.
Post creation commits before the separate EXP helper runs, and helper errors are suppressed.

implementationRisks.impact: Once relationship authorization is added, stale or incompletely authorized state can still feed a separate global helper; partial success also leaves effects inconsistent and complicates verification that all effects occur only after the authorized parent boundary.
implementationRisks.recommendation: Bind gamification to the already-authorized actor and resolved parent, define the intended atomicity/idempotency contract, and ensure no EXP path can re-resolve an unauthorized or mismatched resource.

coverage.assessment: Reviewed authentication, ICS eligibility, role contract, post read, notification creation, and denial/effect ordering. Design has an unresolved ADMIN-versus-all-KX-role authority conflict; baseline remains unimplemented.

Reviewed actor binding, protected input ordering, target-parent resolution, flag creation, and denial behavior. Matrix omits all target resource inputs; baseline creates flags without parent visibility checks.

Reviewed actor-owned follow lookup/toggle, POST and TAG targets, post visibility, institute/course relationship, and error ordering. Target visibility is not implemented, and the matrix does not fully express the protected target chain.

Reviewed moderator aliases, Admin restriction, target resolution, course assignment, transaction effects, flags, and moderation audit binding. Matrix omits target inputs; baseline permits role-only cross-course moderation and caller-controlled audit post association.

Reviewed moderator role/institute eligibility, reporter and target disclosure, course-linked assignment, and global action history. Revised KX_MOD direction is coherent, but baseline remains globally role-scoped and exposes private moderation data without target-course constraints.

Reviewed canonical actor, actor-owned mark-one/mark-all predicates, SUPER_USER/UNKNOWN denial, parsing order, and mutation scope. Ownership predicates are present in baseline, but revised role handling is not implemented.

Reviewed canonical actor, actor-owned notification filters, unread count, serialization, and SUPER_USER/UNKNOWN denial. Actor ownership is present in baseline, but revised role handling is not implemented.

Reviewed postId parent visibility, locked/deleted state, answer creation, notification, anonymous serialization, EXP, and effect ordering. Matrix omits postId; baseline lacks course membership/assignment authorization.

Reviewed all three assigned methods, including post visibility, nested serialization, anonymous identities, authorship, moderator authority, tags/revisions, viewCount, institute/course binding, and denial ordering. Matrix omits postId for every method; baseline GET mutates before authorization and staff DELETE lacks assignment checks.

Reviewed feed scoping/filtering, course visibility, nested author serialization, pagination, creation inputs, institute/course/syllabus/tag binding, transaction effects, and EXP. POST matrix resource inputs are copied from GET rather than its mutation resources; baseline lacks persisted course and child relationship checks.

limitations: Review was confined to the supplied sanitized packet, the ten explicitly assigned route paths, their fourteen assigned HTTP methods, and necessary shared policy sources; no tool, filesystem, network, test, database, or implementation activity was performed.

No separately numbered acceptance-criteria catalog was supplied. affectedAC therefore uses the packet's exact verification case IDs, which are the only operation-specific acceptance identifiers present.

The supplied transactionEvidence field is null. This does not prevent review of these legacy KX routes, which are not oversight-read transaction endpoints, but no runtime transaction behavior is claimed.

The architecture document has no source line numbering. Design findings are anchored to exact assigned route symbols and source lines and identify the conflicting or incomplete operation-matrix fields in their explanations.

Operational META-01 approver, maintainer, production dataset/fingerprint, expiry lifetime, and revocation-runbook identities remain unassigned. Their blocking effect is that production oversight disclosure must remain deny-by-default; no identities or production bindings were inferred. Those assignments are outside these KX route implementations and are not marked resolved.
